documents.title: Academic Honesty Policy
documents.summary: Pomona's Student Handbook academic honesty policy lists 'unapproved use of artificial intelligence' among ways students misrepresent others' ideas or language, leaving approval of AI use to courses. The rest of the document sets the college-wide process for handling any honesty violation: faculty report to the VP of Student Affairs, a preliminary meeting, Academic Discipline Board hearings under a clear-and-convincing standard, and sanctions.

units.anchor: failing to use citations, unapproved use of artificial intelligence
units.policy: In independently prepared projects and assignments, unapproved use of artificial intelligence is an example of intentionally representing the ideas or language of others as one's own.

units.anchor: they must submit a complaint directly to the Vice-President of Student Affairs/Dean of Students
units.policy: A faculty member who believes a student violated academic standards must submit a complaint directly to the Vice-President of Student Affairs/Dean of Students.

units.anchor: All charges must be brought within ten (10) academic days of the discovery
units.policy: All academic dishonesty charges must be brought within ten academic days of the faculty member's discovery of the alleged violation.

units.anchor: schedule a meeting with the student and the faculty member
units.policy: Before any hearing, the Vice-President informs the student of the charge and schedules a preliminary meeting with the student and faculty member, where evidence and possible sanctions are shared.

units.anchor: Any sanctions must be course-specific—such as a failing grade on an assignment.
units.policy: Sanctions in the first-violation process must be course-specific, such as a failing grade on an assignment.

units.anchor: If the violation and resulting penalty could lead to failing the course
units.policy: If the violation and resulting penalty could lead to failing the course, the incident should be referred to a hearing panel.

units.anchor: uses a “clear and convincing” standard to determine responsibility
units.policy: The Academic Discipline Board uses a 'clear and convincing' evidence standard to determine responsibility for violations.

units.anchor: Lower grade on an assignment
units.policy: Academic sanctions may include a lower grade, loss of credit, or an F on an assignment, an F in the course, or make-up work; other sanctions include suspension, loss of honors, or expulsion.

units.anchor: will be reportable to employers, graduate and professional schools
units.policy: For students enrolling from Fall 2026, policy violations and sanctions other than suspension or expulsion are reportable to employers and graduate schools for 3 years after graduation.

documents.title: Computer Science AI Policy Tier System
tiers: Tier 1: See syllabus for allowed usage
Tier 2: Use in any way with required attribution
documents.summary: The Pomona CS department's AI Policy Tier System, piloted in Fall 2026, gives every CS course one of four tiers from no AI at all to completely open use, focusing on usage rather than specific tools. It defines each tier (including spelling-checker and translation edge cases in Tier 0 and collaborator-style attribution in Tier 2) and makes use outside a course's tier a violation of the departmental honor policy.

units.anchor: provide a unified system and increase clarity about what AI usages are allowed or disallowed
units.policy: The document provides a unified system to increase clarity about which AI uses are allowed or disallowed across all Pomona Computer Science classes.

units.anchor: we plan to revisit it regularly
units.policy: The tier system is a pilot program in Fall 2026 that the department plans to revisit regularly.

units.anchor: the document focuses on general usage rather than specific tools
units.policy: Because AI technologies advance rapidly, the document focuses on general usage rather than specific tools (ChatGPT, Gemini, Grammarly, etc.).

units.anchor: outlines the four tiers of allowed use that a course can fall under
units.policy: Each course falls under one of four tiers of allowed use, from least to most permissive: no usage, see syllabus, any use with attribution, completely open use.

units.anchor: it is considered a violation of our Departmental Academic Honor Policy
units.policy: Using AI in a way that does not align with a course's tier is a violation of the Departmental Academic Honor Policy.

units.anchor: Courses in this tier do not allow the use of any AI.
units.policy: (Tier 0) Courses in this tier do not allow the use of any AI.

units.anchor: using generative AI tools to brainstorm ideas, find source materials, summarize ideas, create study guides
units.policy: (Tier 0) Disallowed uses include using generative AI to brainstorm ideas, find source materials, summarize ideas, create study guides, generate code snippets, images, or videos, revise writing, or check work.

units.anchor: Tools that automatically flag spelling and grammatical errors as you write are allowed
units.policy: (Tier 0) Tools that automatically flag spelling and grammar errors as you write (e.g., Microsoft Word's checkers) are allowed.

units.anchor: not tools that offer suggested revisions of your sentences (for example, Grammarly)
units.policy: (Tier 0) Tools that offer suggested revisions of sentences, such as Grammarly, are not allowed.

units.anchor: If English is not your first language, please ask your instructor about whether tools
units.policy: (Tier 0) Students whose first language is not English should ask their instructor whether translation tools are allowed.

units.anchor: allow some flexibility for instructors who primarily want to curb AI use
units.policy: (Tier 1) The tier gives flexibility to instructors who primarily want to curb AI use but may make exceptions tailored to their course's learning objectives.

units.anchor: might allow the use of AI for study purposes
units.policy: (Tier 1 example) A course might allow AI for study purposes (clarifying questions, additional examples, study guides) but prohibit it while completing assignments and exams.

units.anchor: students must read the course syllabus carefully and discuss allowed uses with their instructor
units.policy: (Tier 1) Students must read the course syllabus carefully and discuss allowed uses with their instructor.

units.anchor: openly allow students to use generative AI tools in their learning
units.policy: (Tier 2) The goal is to openly allow students to use generative AI tools in their learning.

units.anchor: they should be credited in the same way that you would share authorship
units.policy: (Tier 2) If generative AI plays a significant role in the genesis of work, it should be credited as one would share authorship with a collaborating lab partner in a publication.

units.anchor: The course syllabus will contain more information on expectations and attribution formatting.
units.policy: (Tier 2) The course syllabus will contain more information on expectations and attribution formatting.

units.anchor: Students can freely use generative AI tools
units.policy: (Tier 3) Students can freely use generative AI tools.

units.anchor: do not need to credit their use
units.policy: (Tier 3) Students do not need to credit their use of generative AI tools.

units.anchor: generated by a student using an AI system are treated as the student's own work
units.policy: (Tier 3 only) Text and images a student generates with an AI system are treated as the student's own work for the College Academic Honesty Policy.

documents.title: Academic Honesty Policy (Computer Science Department)
documents.summary: The CS department's academic honesty policy requires independent work not based on unapproved sources, including AI tools, and makes the department's AI Policy Tier System binding on all CS courses, with exceptions set in syllabi. It bans copying solutions from AI, requires citation of AI in papers where permitted, forbids prompting AI with course materials unless allowed, describes similarity and AI-content detection, and states escalating penalties.

units.anchor: information obtained from sources other than those approved by the instructors, including AI tools
units.policy: Submitted work must not be based on help from others or information from sources other than those approved by the instructors, including AI tools.

units.anchor: will appear in the course syllabus or the instructions for an assignment
units.policy: Any exceptions or differences from the department's general understanding of academic honesty appear in the course syllabus or assignment instructions.

units.anchor: launched a pilot AI Policy Tier System that all Computer Science courses will now follow
units.policy: Starting Fall 2026, all Computer Science courses follow the department's pilot AI Policy Tier System.

units.anchor: it is considered a violation of our Departmental Academic Honor Policy
units.policy: Using AI in a way that does not align with a course's tier is a violation of the Departmental Academic Honor Policy.

units.anchor: Ask your instructor if you are ever unsure about what constitutes acceptable behavior.
Copying solutions from any source, including the web, AI tools, or students who took previous
units.policy: Copying solutions from any source, including the web, AI tools, or students from previous offerings, is not allowed.

units.anchor: use software and other tools to detect similarities between submissions and generative AI content
units.policy: The department routinely uses software and other tools to detect similarities between submissions and generative AI content.

units.anchor: Identical, or nearly identical, submissions will be considered conclusive evidence of plagiarism.
The prose must be your own
units.policy: When papers are assigned, the prose must be the student's own.

units.anchor: all external sources, including AI tools, if permitted, must be properly cited
units.policy: In papers, all external sources, including AI tools where permitted, must be properly cited.

units.anchor: you should never use course materials or assignments as a prompt for an AI tool
units.policy: Students should never use course materials or assignments as a prompt for an AI tool unless explicitly allowed by the course policy.

units.anchor: Graders who encounter suspicious similarities between submissions must report those instances
units.policy: Graders who encounter suspicious similarities between submissions must report them to the course instructor.

units.anchor: Suspected violations are always reported to the Dean of Students Office.
A first offense results in a zero and no less than a half-letter-grade reduction.
A second offense is automatically referred to the College's Academic Discipline Board.
the Department will recommend a failing grade in the course
units.policy: For a second offense in the same course, the department recommends a failing grade in the course.

documents.title: CS51: Introduction to Computer Science, Fall 2026 (course website, Academic Integrity section)
documents.summary: CS 51 places itself in Tier 1 of the department's AI tier system and, while encouraging collaboration among classmates and staff, forbids material from any external source, explicitly including AI tools such as Copilot, Claude, and ChatGPT. Course materials may not be submitted to AI tools, and violations bring reporting to the Dean, a zero, and a half-letter-grade reduction, with a hearing for a second incident.

units.anchor: CS51 is Tier 1 within the Computer Science AI Policy Tier System
This includes AI tools, such as coPilot, Claude, and chatGPT.
units.policy: Using material from any external source, including AI tools such as coPilot, Claude, and chatGPT, is forbidden.

units.anchor: The actual solutions to the assignments you submit must be your own
units.policy: The solutions students submit must be their own (and their partner's, if applicable).

units.anchor: If you have any questions about what is appropriate or inappropriate collaboration, please speak
units.policy: Students with questions about appropriate collaboration should speak with the instructors.

units.anchor: When in doubt, credit your sources.
This includes submitting them to AI tools for assistance.
units.policy: Course materials, including graded assignments and checkpoint/exam summaries, must not be published or distributed, including by submitting them to AI tools for assistance.

units.anchor: immediate reporting to the Dean of the Students, a zero in the assignment/exam
units.policy: Failing to adhere to the guidelines results in immediate reporting to the Dean of Students, a zero on the assignment/exam, and a half-letter-grade reduction.

units.anchor: A second incident will result in a hearing panel and a recommendation for failing
units.policy: A second incident results in a hearing panel and a recommendation for failing the course.

documents.title: CS 62 Data Structures and Advanced Programming, Fall 2026 Syllabus
documents.summary: CS 62 adopts Tier 1 of the department's AI tier system: students write all code themselves in VS Code without AI tools installed, and AI may not be used on assignments in any way, including generating or debugging code. AI is allowed only for studying for exams, e.g., explanations of course topics or generating sample questions.

units.anchor: This class will use Tier 1, which means that appropriate usage is defined below
units.policy: The class uses Tier 1 of the department's AI tier system, with appropriate usage defined in the syllabus.

units.anchor: without any additional tools beyond VS Code (without AI tools installed)
units.policy: Students should write all their code on their own without any additional tools beyond VS Code, without AI tools installed.

units.anchor: should not be used on the assignments in this class in any way
units.policy: AI tools should not be used on the assignments in the class in any way.

units.anchor: either to generate code or to assist you in debugging code
units.policy: AI tools should not be used on assignments to assist in debugging code.

units.anchor: You may use it to help you study for exams
units.policy: Students may use AI to study for exams, e.g., to explain a topic covered in class or to generate sample questions.

units.anchor: If you are ever unsure about what constitutes acceptable collaboration, please ask!
your work must not be based on information obtained from sources other than those approved
units.policy: Students' work must not be based on information from sources other than those approved for the course (the text, linked web pages, lecture materials).

documents.title: CS105, Fall 2026 (course website, AI Policy)
documents.summary: CS 105 adopts Tier 0 of the department's AI tier system: no AI use at all, including brainstorming, summarizing, study guides, code snippets, revising writing, or checking work, with only automatic spelling/grammar flagging allowed. The stated rationale is that out-of-class help should target learning, so students should use the professor and TAs rather than AI tools.

units.anchor: this class maintains the Tier 0 level of acceptable AI use
Courses in this tier do not allow the use of any AI.
units.policy: CS 105, as a Tier 0 course, does not allow the use of any AI.

units.anchor: using generative AI tools to brainstorm ideas, find source materials, summarize ideas, create study guides
units.policy: Disallowed uses include using generative AI to brainstorm ideas, find source materials, summarize ideas, create study guides, generate code snippets, images, or videos, revise writing, or check work.

units.anchor: Tools that automatically flag spelling and grammatical errors as you write are allowed
not tools that offer suggested revisions of your sentences (for example, Grammarly)
units.policy: Tools that offer suggested revisions of sentences, such as Grammarly, are not allowed.

units.anchor: If English is not your first language, please ask your instructor about whether tools
units.policy: Students whose first language is not English should ask the instructor whether translation tools are allowed.

units.anchor: ensure that your out-of-class help is targeted towards your learning
units.policy: The principle behind applying Tier 0 is to ensure students' out-of-class help is targeted toward their learning.

units.anchor: use your professor and TAs as the primary resource for out-of-class help
units.policy: Students are to use the professor and TAs, rather than AI tools, as the primary resource for out-of-class help.

notes: Coder B. Student Handbook: the only AI-specific text is the 'unapproved use of artificial intelligence' clause; a small set of the general academic-dishonesty procedures that govern how such a violation is handled (reporting, preliminary meeting, standard of evidence, sanctions, reportability) were coded as enforcement units; the rest of the hearing procedure (panel membership, hearing rules, appeals) was treated as non-AI boilerplate and not coded. CS 51/62/105 each adopt a tier from the department's AI Policy Tier System; their stances reflect the tier as applied (CS 51 Tier 1 but forbids AI tools; CS 62 Tier 1 restricted to studying; CS 105 Tier 0).
